title: Stop Making These 3 Common Mistakes!
summary: In this short lesson, you will learn how to avoid three very common English mistakes. By the end, you will speak and write more clearly.

sections.h: Saying 'I am agree' instead of 'I agree'
sections.p: Many students think 'agree' is an adjective like 'happy', so they say 'I am agree'. But 'agree' is a verb. In English, we do not use the verb 'to be' before 'agree'. Just say 'I agree' when you have the same opinion as someone else.

ex.mean: I have the same opinion as you.

sections.p: These two words are very easy to mix up. When you take something from someone to use and return later, you borrow it. When you give something to someone for a short time, you lend it. Remember: borrow takes, lend gives.

ex.mean: Can I take your pen and give it back later?

ex.en: Can you lend me ten dollars?
ex.mean: Can you give me ten dollars for a short time?

sections.p: People often use these words for the same thing, but they are different. 'Funny' means something makes you laugh, like a good joke. 'Fun' means an activity is enjoyable and you like doing it.

ex.en: That comedy movie was very funny.
ex.mean: The movie made me laugh a lot.
Learning English is an enjoyable activity.

tip: Make flashcards with the correct pairs on one side and your native language on the other. Review them for five minutes every day.

quiz.en: Please ___ me your jacket for the evening.
The clown at the party was very ___.
We had a lot of ___ at the beach yesterday.

quiz.ask: Find the mistake in this sentence: 'She am agree with the plan.'
quiz.en: She am agree with the plan.
